key_insight: The paper shows that verifiable environments can be built like LEGO bricks: small, trusted tasks can be recursively composed into many harder environments. This removes the usual linear scaling bottleneck and helps RL generalize reasoning better.
problem_solved: It addresses the difficulty of scaling verifiable RL environments for LLM reasoning. Manual or one-by-one environment creation does not scale well, so the training signal remains limited and reasoning generalization stalls.
method: Introduces RACES: Recursive Automated Composition for Environment Scaling.
Automatically composes existing verifiable environments into new, more complex ones through recursive reuse of components.
Expands environment diversity without requiring fully manual construction of each new task.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a scalable way to generate richer training environments for reasoning-focused RL. It can improve data efficiency, reduce environment design cost, and support stronger generalization beyond seen tasks.
visual_elements: LEGO-style block diagram showing small environments composed into larger ones
Recursive tree/graph illustration of environment composition over multiple levels
Before-vs-after scaling chart comparing manual construction vs recursive composition
Pipeline icon sequence: base tasks -> composition -> new environments -> improved reasoning
paper_title: Verifiable Environments Are LEGO Bricks: Recursive Composition for Reasoning Generalization
paper_authors: Hao Xiang, Qiaoyu Tang, Le Yu, Yaojie Lu, Xianpei Han
